'''Eric C. Torrence''' (born 1968) is an American experimental particle [[physicist]] at the [[University of Oregon]] who conducts research on [[elementary particle]]s and fields.

== Early life and education ==

Eric Torrence complete his Bachelor of Science degree at the [[University of Washington]] in 1990. He earned his Ph.D. at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in June 1997, with his dissertation, ''Search for Anomalous Couplings in the Decay of Polarized Z Bosons to Tau Lepton Pairs'', advised by [[Richard K. Yamamoto]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Torrence |first=Eric C. |date=May 22, 1997 |title=Search for Anomalous Couplings in the Decay of Polarized Z Bosons to Tau Lepton Pairs |url=https://www.slac.stanford.edu/pubs/slacreports/reports06/slac-r-509.pdf |journal=SLAC-Report-509 |via=National Technical Information Service, U.S. Department of Commerce}}</ref>

== Career and research ==

Eric Torrence joined the Physics Department at the University of Oregon in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eric Torrence {{!}} College of Arts and Sciences |url=https://cas.uoregon.edu/directory/cas-natural-sciences-faculty/all/torrence |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=cas.uoregon.edu}}</ref> An experimental particle physicist, he uses [[particle accelerator]]s to study basic properties of matter and fundamental forces of nature. He has conducted research at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] and [[FASER experiment|FASER]] collaborations at [[CERN]] in Switzerland, and he is a member of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eric Torrence Research Interests |url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/torrence/research.shtml |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=pages.uoregon.edu}}</ref>

* Jeffery A. Kolb<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kolb |first=Jeffery A. |title=A search for neutrinoless tau decays to three leptons |date=June 2008 |publisher=University of Oregon |id={{ProQuest|3325664}}}}</ref>
* John Myers<ref>{{Cite book|last=Myers |first=John |date=2019-09-18 |title=Search for Higgs Boson Pair Production in the bbWW* Channel in SQRT(S) = 13 TeV Proton-Proton Collisions at the Large Hadron Collider Using the Atlas Detector |url=https://hdl.handle.net/1794/24908 |language=en-US}}</ref>
* Rahmat Rhamat<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rahmat |first=Rahmat |title=Hadronic spectrum of tau lepton to antipion-neutral pion-tau neutrino decays |publisher=University of Oregon |year=2008 |id={{ProQuest|3335198}}}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* 2008 University of Oregon Faculty Excellence Award. The university's ''Physics Newsletter'' reported that Torrence's "leading role today in the [[Tau (particle)|tau physics]] efforts of the [[ATLAS experiment]] places him at the center of physics in the coming decade."<ref>{{Cite news |date=Spring 2009 |editor-last=Brau |editor-first=James E. |editor-link=James E. Brau |title=Physics Professors Eric Torrence and Hailin Wang Honored with Faculty Excellence Awards |url=https://bpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/blogs.uoregon.edu/dist/0/5172/files/2013/12/Physics_News_2009s-1sebqnb.pdf |work=Physics Newsletter |pages=1, 2}}</ref>
* 2022 [[Don Tykeson|Tykeson]] Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching.  Hal Sadofsky, divisional dean for the natural sciences, said, "Professor Torrence's attention to his students and their success, while he pursues a highly active and visible research program, epitomize the ideals of the teacher-scholar."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-03-11 |title=UO honors 3 faculty members with Tykeson Teaching Awards |url=https://news.uoregon.edu/content/uo-honors-3-faculty-members-tykeson-teaching-awards |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=OregonNews |language=en}}</ref>
* 2024 Fellow, [[American Physical Society]], cited ''For significant contributions with the ATLAS and [[FASER experiment|FASER]] Collaborations, particularly in the searches for new physics, measurement of the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] luminosity, and for leadership in the operations of both experiments.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=eric%20torrence&af=true |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
